extraction.name: NWPU-RESISC45
extraction.description: A large-scale benchmark dataset for REmote Sensing Image Scene Classification (RESISC), containing 31,500 images covering 45 scene classes with 700 images in each class.
extraction.creator: Gong Cheng, Junwei Han, Xiaoqiang Lu
extraction.citeAs: Gong Cheng, Junwei Han, and Xiaoqiang Lu, "Remote Sensing Image Scene Classification: Benchmark and State of the Art," Proceedings of the IEEE, 2016.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was extracted by experts in the field of remote sensing image interpretation from Google Earth. Images were carefully selected under various weather, season, illumination, imaging conditions, and scales to ensure rich variations.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were cropped to a size of 256x256 pixels in the RGB color space.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Scene classes were selected by investigating existing datasets and searching literature keywords. The dataset covers 45 scene classes including land use, land cover, man-made objects, and landscape nature objects. Labels are assigned based on these predefined semantic classes.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Experts in the field of remote sensing image interpretation
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables the community to develop and evaluate various data-driven algorithms, particularly deep learning methods, for remote sensing image scene classification, which has applications in natural hazards detection, land use determination, and urban planning.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset covers more than 100 countries and regions, including developing, transition, and highly developed economies. However, it lacks diversity in some existing datasets which mainly cover specific regions like China or the US.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Existing datasets prior to this work had limitations such as small scale of scene classes and image numbers, lack of image variations and diversity, and saturation of accuracy. This dataset aims to address these but is still limited to overhead imagery and does not incorporate social media or ground-level photo data.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Benchmarking of state-of-the-art scene classification methods.
